F: external force; M: moment about a stated point; r: lever-arm vector; w: force per length; W: resultant force; x: position. Resultant location is undefined if W = 0.
N: axial force; V: shear force; A: section area; As: shear area; m: number of equally loaded shear planes; d: pin/hole diameter; t: plate thickness; delta: extension; L: gauge length.
E: Young's modulus; G: shear modulus; K: bulk modulus; nu: Poisson ratio; Sy: yield strength; A0 and L0: original dimensions. Energy per volume has stress units.
N(x): signed axial force; E(x), A(x): local modulus and area; alpha: thermal expansion coefficient; delta T: temperature change; rho: mass density; g: gravity; k: axial stiffness.
ki: member axial stiffness Ei Ai/Li; Pi: member force; delta: common displacement. Parallel-bar load sharing assumes rigid end plates, engaged members and compatible axial movement.
Ix, Iy: second moments about named centroidal axes; Ixy: product moment; d: parallel-axis offset (diameter in the shape table); c: extreme-fiber distance; rg: radius of gyration.
T: torque; r: radial location; J: polar moment for a circular section; G: shear modulus; phi: twist in radians; n: rpm; omega: rad/s; power is in W when T is N m.
V: internal shear; M: internal bending moment; w: downward load per length; x: coordinate to the right; L: span; a and b: distances from point load to the two supports.
M: bending moment; y: coordinate from the neutral axis, positive upward; I: centroidal principal second moment; Z: elastic section modulus; N: signed axial force.
Q: first moment of the selected partial area about the neutral axis; b: local width; q: shear flow in force/length; s: connector spacing. Q is not the second moment I.
v: upward-positive deflection; theta: slope; E: modulus; I: bending-axis second moment; L: beam length. P and w are downward load magnitudes in the tables.
p: internal-minus-external pressure; r: vessel mean radius; t: wall thickness. For springs D: mean coil diameter; d: wire diameter; na: active turns; Cs: spring index.
sigma x, sigma y, tau xy: stress components at one point; theta: counterclockwise axes rotation; C: circle center; R: circle radius. Use atan2 to retain quadrant information.
epsilon0, epsilon45, epsilon90: measured directional strains; gamma xy: engineering shear strain; E, nu, G: isotropic constants; alpha delta T: stress-free thermal strain.
sigma1, sigma2, sigma3: principal stresses at one point; Sy: yield strength; sigma eq: chosen equivalent stress; ny: nominal yield factor. Criteria here concern ductile static yielding.
U: elastic strain energy; ks: shear correction factor; m: bending moment due to a unit virtual force. Impact W is weight (force), h is drop height and k is spring stiffness.
Rj: redundant reactions; fij: displacement at coordinate i per unit force at coordinate j; Delta i: specified support displacement. Signs follow the chosen positive coordinates.
Pcr: ideal critical compression; Imin: weakest relevant second moment; K: effective-length factor; lambda: slenderness; rg: radius of gyration; e: eccentricity; c: extreme-fiber distance.
Iyz: centroidal product of area; u,v: principal-axis coordinates; Iu,Iv: corresponding second moments. Mu = integral(v sigma x dA); Mv = -integral(u sigma x dA).
r: radius from initial center of curvature; rn: neutral radius; rc: centroid radius; e = rc - rn; A: area. Positive M causes inner-fiber tension in the declared convention.
a,b: inner/outer radii; pi,po: positive pressure magnitudes; C,D: Lame constants; r: wall radius; ur(r): radial displacement. Pressure gives compressive radial stress.
Jt: torsion constant, not generally the polar moment; b,t: strip width/thickness; Am: median-line enclosed area; q: circulating shear flow; s: wall arc length.
Sa (written sigma a): amplitude; sigma m: mean; Se: appropriate component fatigue strength; Sut: tensile ultimate strength; Y: crack geometry factor; a: specified crack size; T: kelvin in creep.
Ze,Zp: elastic and plastic section moduli; yp: plastic neutral axis; My,Mp: first-yield/fully-plastic moments; Sy: ideal symmetric yield strength. Pure bending is assumed.
Ei,Ai,Ici: layer modulus, area and centroidal second moment; yE: elastic neutral axis; Vf,Vm: fiber/matrix volume fractions; E1,E2,G12,nu12,nu21: orthotropic lamina properties.
u: displacement vector; b: body force per volume; C: elasticity tensor; I: identity tensor; ke,K: element/global stiffness matrices; F: load vector. The bar element is a 1D idealization.
